title: Ang 137–145: Majh ki Var
hookLine: Guru Nanak's ballad in Majh, first half
tomorrow: what would a mosque built out of mercy look like?

cards: A package lands on your porch with your street on it and a stranger's name. A cashier hands back a twenty when you paid with a ten. A paycheck has a few extra hours you never worked.
Nobody would ever know. So what's the one thing that's never yours to take? Guru Nanak's Majh ki Var, which opens on ang 137, has a line for exactly this, and it speaks to two neighbors at once.

teach.h: THE GURU, A HOUSE OF COOL SNOW.
teach.b: Majh ki Var is Guru Nanak's ballad in Majh, built like the first var, saloks set before pauris.

Its very first salok, on ang 137, praises the Guru, in paraphrase: the Guru is the giver, the Guru is a house of cool snow, the Guru is the lamp of the three worlds. Cool, when everything's heating up.
A few pages on, ang 141, comes a line about money and what isn't yours.
In paraphrase: to take what is rightfully another's, Nanak says, is pork to the Muslim and beef to the Hindu.
He reaches each neighbor with their own deepest line, the food they'd never touch, and lays it over taking what isn't yours.
Then he keeps going, in paraphrase: the Guru and the guide will stand by you only if you don't eat what's dead.
Talk alone won't get you to heaven; you're freed by living the truth. Truth, lived, from ang 62, again. So what does this give you for a week like this one?
A bright line, not a debate. Not, is it really stealing if they made the mistake.
If not, it's off the plate, whoever's watching or not.

how: Majh ki Var is sung in kirtan and read in order after the Barah Maha; some Sikhs quote its ang 141 salok on 'another's due' when speaking of honest earning, kirat karni.

games.q: inside the Majh ballad — tap the pairs.
p: the Guru, a house of cool snow
another's due: pork to one, beef to the other

s: the ang 141 salok is a rule about food
it borrows each neighbor's strongest food line to say: what's another's due is never yours.
Majh ki Var opens by calling the Guru a house of cool snow
the giver, the cool house, the lamp of the three worlds.

games.q: a self-checkout scans your bag of apples as one apple. the line is long and nobody noticed. what does ang 141 say?
o: the store made the mistake, so the cost is on the store.
what's another's due is off the plate: fix it and pay.
it evens out; stores overcharge people all the time.
games.why: Guru Nanak's line asks one question, is it rightfully mine? and the salok goes on: talk alone won't free you; living the truth does.

practice: If you can, read one salok of Majh ki Var first. Then look around for one thing near you that isn't yours: a borrowed charger, a sibling's hoodie, a library book, a neighbor's container.
Set it by the door, or wherever its owner will find it, and sit the rest of the time with your hands open and empty.
